title: Count the steps — Savile Row to Pall Mall
learning_goal: Know that Fogg's 1,151 steps are about a kilometre of real London, and that the street they end in is clubland — gas-lit since 1807, with the Reform, the Travellers and the Athenaeum in a row.

narration.script: Half past eleven. Fogg leaves the house and walks to his club. He counts his steps as he goes: one thousand one hundred and fifty-one of them. His way runs down Savile Row, right into Burlington Gardens, then left down Old Bond Street to Piccadilly. Across the road, and down the long slope of St James's Street. At the bottom he turns east, into Pall Mall. From his front door to the club door is one thousand one hundred and twenty metres: about one kilometre. So each step is about ninety-seven centimetres. He never hurries. And this is the street he is walking into. Pall Mall had gas lamps in 1807, one of the first streets in London. Sixty-five years before Fogg, the lamps here were already the future. This is clubland: a row of private clubs on the south side. Three of them stand together. In front of us, the grand stone front with the tall windows: 104 Pall Mall, the Reform Club, by Charles Barry, opened 1841. That one is Fogg's. A little to the left, No. 106, the Travellers, Barry's first Italian palazzo, finished in 1832. And beyond it, No. 107, the Athenaeum. One turn of the head covers all three.

media.note: THE COUNTING BEAT (D6). The step count is told over the plan, not over a street the traveller has to steer. Treatment asked for, and deliberately unlike scene 12's use of the same plate: crop to the West End quarter only (roughly Regent Street to Green Park, Oxford Street to Pall Mall) so the street names are readable, and draw the route in FIVE short strokes that stop at each turn — Savile Row · Burlington Gardens · Old Bond Street · Piccadilly · St James's Street · Pall Mall — with the running step number stamped beside each turn (67 · 208 · 405 · 629 · 789 · 1,151, F-43). Scene 12 keeps the whole plate and one continuous line at cab speed. Until the crop exists (request to Content Preparer: M-30a, a free PD derivative) the film shows the full plate under a slow Ken Burns and the captions carry the turns.

production_notes: TRANSPORT SCENE (D6, 2026-08-19 restructure). This was the seven-stop Street View walk; D6 rules that Street View is a stop-and-look device and never transport, so the walk is gone: no interaction, no route, no 'tap to step', nothing to aim. The scene is now two beats. BEAT A, 0–~40 s: the counting, over the 1872 plan (M-30) — the numbers and the turns live on the map. BEAT B, ~40–94 s: the street simply plays while the guide talks clubland. In the FILM beat B is the cached open-imagery walk (visual kind `panowalk`, stops 5 then 6 of this scene's geometry: St James's × Pall Mall, then the 158 m up to the Reform door — Mapillary 360° frames, 2024, CC BY-SA platform default, see studio/tools/panowalk/README.md), with the `camera` cue below stopping the walk in front of the Reform as the guide names it, and the two neighbours named over their own façades (M-69b, M-69a). In the PLAYER beat B is the M-01 embed (Pall Mall, `use: player`), which plays by itself. NEITHER track asks the traveller to do anything. The seven `streetview` media entries are GEOMETRY ONLY: they are the survey points the pano cache is indexed against (waypoint_index 0…6 = count-the-steps-w00…w06) and the anchors of the route drawn on M-30; nothing Google is shown or recorded here. They must stay seven, in this order, or `panomove.planScene` re-indexes and the cut sheet's `stops: [5]` / `[6]` point at the wrong place. The `camera` track is kept because the linear renderer's panowalk reads it (render_linear.mjs → buildPanowalk → panomove.planScene) on any scene type; the validator's 'camera track on a video scene … will be ignored' warning is therefore stale — Engine backlog. Only TWO camera cues, deliberately: a first pass gave the Travellers and the Athenaeum their own look_at cues and `panomove.frameForCue` answered them with frames 36 m and 96 m BACK down the street, so the walk visibly reversed twice at the end. The cue that survives is the one that ends the walk (arrive, stop, look at 104); the neighbours are stills. Cue times are in scene seconds and must stay inside their stop's window: with duration_s 94, panomove.planScene puts stop 5 at 56.4 s and stop 6 at 67.7 s, so 57 belongs to stop 5 and 79 to stop 6. They are then re-scaled onto the cut sheet's segment lengths, which is why each label also gives the second it lands on in the FILM (43.5 s and 64 s of a 90.2 s scene) — that is the number to check against the narration, and the reason the cue seconds do not read like the spoken seconds. If duration_s, the script or the cut sheet's `dur`s change, re-derive both. Words: everything the walk used to carry is still here — 1,151 steps, the kilometre, 'he never hurries', gas from 1807, the three clubs — only re-homed so that nothing depends on the traveller steering a camera. Left / right is never spoken: the film's open imagery travels EAST and the player's M-01 travels WEST, so the clubs are named by side of the street ('the south side'). Basis for 'the south side', for the Fact-Checker: F-18 gives the addresses (Athenaeum 107, Travellers 106, Reform 104) and the OSM centroids this scene already carries — 51.50654,-0.13346 · 51.50668,-0.13308 · 51.50679,-0.13275 — all sit south of the Pall Mall carriageway; it is the same claim scene 05 made as 'watch the left side' for a westbound shot. Engine request (one line each, not done here): the player should honour media windows in a `video` scene so beat A shows M-30 before the embed starts; and validate.py should stop warning about `camera` on non-streetview scenes now that panowalk reads it. Retired with this pass: scene 05 pall-mall-pass, which existed only as the linear stand-in for the walk (its words are these words). M-69a / M-69b (Athenaeum and Travellers façades) come with it and are wired here.

Sources unchanged. | A11 content-preparer 2026-09-03 (spell-break sweep, founder's instruction): TWO MEDIA SWAPS, no words changed. (1) M-20 -> M-104. The M-20 façade still (Philip Cornwall, geograph 6571401, 2019) was shot during a Brexit demonstration: EU flags on poles and hand-painted placards with legible slogans fill the lower half of a 3024x4032 portrait frame. It was the declared fallback for panowalk stop 6 here and the opening picture of scene 06, so contemporary protest recurred through a chapter set in 1872 — exactly what brief.md's must-not list excludes ('politics of the day beyond a line'). Replaced by M-104 (File:Reform Club 02.JPG, Philafrenzy 2015, 4000x3000, CC BY-SA 4.0): the whole palazzo in sunlight from the Carlton Gardens corner, which is also what the line actually describes ('the Portland-stone front with the tall windows'). M-20 is marked REJECTED in media/manifest.md so nobody re-adds it. (2) M-69b -> M-106. Looked at the pixels of every façade in this scene and found that the geograph file titled 'Travellers Club, Pall Mall' (5323789) is not the Travellers Club: it is the Reform Club photographed from the west, identified by the 'CARLTON GARDENS SW1' street sign on its near corner (Carlton Gardens meets Pall Mall at 51.50665,-0.13398, against the Reform's OSM footprint corner at 51.50659,-0.13381; the Travellers' OSM centroid is 51.50668,-0.13308, 65 m east and on no corner), and by the building itself — three storeys of grey Portland stone, red pantile roof, Greek-fret string course, alternating triangular and segmental pediments, all matching M-69c/M-104/M-102 and none of them matching the Travellers' two storeys of cream stucco under an anthemion frieze. The film therefore said 'No. 106, the Travellers' over a picture of No. 104. Replaced by M-106 (File:Travellers Club, London.jpg, Matt Brown 2006, 800x600, CC BY 2.0), which is the Travellers' Pall Mall front. Honest limits of the new picture: 800x600 (comparable to M-69a's 640x501, so a gentle move only, never a punch-in) and there is scaffolding at both edges of the frame. No narration, overlay, camera cue or duration changed.
